asset: the chain hoist on the loading dock

messages.content:
The chain hoist brake is slipping. Load drifts down after release.
Evidence (work-order history): same issue on 2026-05-22 (stopped drift, ran fine) and 2026-07-01 (adjusted brake, seemed OK). Both times we didn't find why it started slipping.

Per the provided work-order history: this is the third occurrence, and the two prior closures ('adjusted brake' and 'stopped drift') mean the root cause was never found — treat this as one recurring problem, not a new one. Safety floor: de-energize and apply LOTO before inspecting the brake assembly; no energized work. Next step: measure the brake shoe wear, friction-surface temperature, and any oil contamination on the pads — capture those readings in photo or notes — so the root cause stops hiding behind the same adjustment.

pump is cavitating again today. sucking air. priming does not help.
Evidence (work-order history): 2026-06-10 primed and ran, 2026-06-25 bled air and reset, today same noise. nothing written about what causes the air entry.

Per the provided work-order history: this is the third air event, and the priors (primed, bled, reset) point to a symptom fix — the reason the pump keeps drawing air was never diagnosed. Safety floor: de-energize and lockout before opening any line or fitting; no pressurized work. Next step: check inlet line integrity for cracks or loose fittings, verify the suction strainer is not clogged, and note the fluid level in the reservoir — capture photos of all three — so you know whether this is a leak, starvation, or blockage.

Resistor thermal cutout fired again. Second time this shift. Rebooted drives, came back up.
Evidence (work-order history): 2026-07-15 reset the thermal and ran 8 hours OK. 2026-07-19 same shutdown, cleared the fault, no notes on thermal cause.

Per the provided work-order history: the two resets without diagnosis means the reason the resistor is overheating — whether brake duty is too high or cooling is blocked — was never captured. Treat this as one recurring thermal issue, not two separate faults. Safety floor: de-energize the drive and braking circuit, apply LOTO before touching the resistor; no live braking work. Next step: touch the resistor case with your hand (after it cools) to gauge surface temperature, inspect the resistor fins for dust or blockage, and note if brake command frequency is high — photo or quick note of all three — so you know if the resistor is just undersized, clogged, or being asked to brake too often.

Vibrator is chattering, sounds like a jackhammer. Happens soon into run. Just started today.
Evidence (work-order history): Same chatter 2026-05-09, cleared by toggling the solenoid. Again 2026-06-14, toggled and ok. No mention of what was causing it.

Per the provided work-order history: the chatter events, and every prior fix was a toggle — the mechanical or electrical reason the armature chattered was never identified. Treat this as one unresolved vibration problem. Safety floor: de-energize the solenoid circuit and apply LOTO before removing covers; no energized maintenance. Next step: with power off, manually lift the armature and release it several times to feel for mechanical stiction or roughness, check the air gap at rest with a feeler gauge, and listen for any debris rattle inside the housing — write down the feel and any clinking sound — so you know if this is a seizure risk, a gap misalignment, or loose armature rattle.

Sump is backing up. Drain line is blocked again. Need to flush it out.
Evidence (work-order history): flushed out the line 2026-04-18 (worked), flushed again 2026-06-02 (worked), flushed today. No notes on why material keeps plugging it.

Per the provided work-order history: the flush-outs over weeks represent not random blockage — the root cause of the clogging pattern was never investigated. Treat the whole cycle as one recurring obstruction problem. Safety floor: de-energize the centrifuge and pump, apply LOTO before breaking any line; no pressurized work. Next step: after flushing, collect a sample of the debris that came out (even a spoonful) and note the line internal diameter and any visible corrosion or weld beads that could trap solids — photo the debris and any rough spots — so you know if the line is undersized, corroded, or the process is sending denser material than designed.

Air pressure is dropping off again. Should be 90 psi, reading 75. Last time I just turned the screw back up.
Evidence (work-order history): 2026-06-30 pressure drift, adjusted the regulator up, held for a day. 2026-07-10 same drift, adjusted and OK. Today drifting again.

Per the provided work-order history: the pressure drifts with adjustments means the regulator is leaking set pressure, not just needing tweaking. The leak path — whether the diaphragm is torn or the seat is clogged — was never found. Treat this as one regulator failure that keeps hiding in the adjustment. Safety floor: bleed the air system to zero pressure, apply tag-out and LOTO; no pressurized work. Next step: measure how long the pressure holds after you set it to 90 psi and turn the input off (does it stay stable or drop fast?), listen for hissing from the exhaust port, and inspect the diaphragm for cracking when you crack the main cap — write the hold time, whether you hear exhaust leak, and what the diaphragm looks like — so you know if you are chasing a failed seal or a contaminated valve seat.

Compressor won't unload. Pressure keeps climbing. Bled the valve yesterday and it dropped, back up high today.
Evidence (work-order history): 2026-07-08 bled the unload, pressure dropped. 2026-07-18 high pressure, bled again.

Per the provided work-order history: the bleeding in weeks means the unload pilot does not hold — the reason was never diagnosed. Treat as one valve leakage. Safety floor: de-pressurize and apply LOTO and bleed tag; no pressurized components. Next step: cycle the unload valve arm and feel for grinding, inspect the outlet vent line for oil, check if the pilot line is kinked — document arm feel, vent condition, pilot path — so you know if stuck spool, blocked vent, or cracked line.

Mill motor is vibrating badly. Tightened all the bolts last month and it was smooth, but shaking again now.
Evidence (work-order history): 2026-06-15 tightened bolts, vibration gone. 2026-07-25 heavy vibration again. No notes on why bolts keep coming loose.

Per the provided work-order history: the bolts loosening in weeks means something works them free — whether resonance, missing lock washer, or under-torque was never found. Treat as one mounting problem. Safety floor: de-energize motor and apply LOTO; no live work. Next step: torque every bolt to spec (write the value), mark one bolt with witness line to check rotation, verify lock washers present — sketch the bolt circle with condition notes — so you know if under-torque, missing locks, or resonance.

Load cell zero is drifting again. Hopper shows false weight even with inlet empty. Sent a zero command like last time.
Evidence (work-order history): 2026-05-20 cell drifted, zeroed, worked. 2026-07-03 same drift, zeroed, no investigation.

Per the provided work-order history: the zero drifts in weeks means the sensor itself is creeping — the temperature, humidity, or stress causing drift was never captured. Treat as one stability problem. Safety floor: de-energize scale system and tag hopper controls; no live measurement work. Next step: next time it drifts, record ambient temperature and humidity, photo cell and cable for damage, check mounting looseness — log temp/humidity and routing — so you know if thermal creep, moisture ingress, or mechanical strain.

Gear is making that grinding noise again. Sounds like metal on metal. Let it run and it stopped after warm-up.
Evidence (work-order history): 2026-06-08 same grinding on startup, smooth after warm. 2026-06-28 grinding again, warmed up. No notes on cold-start cause.

Per the provided work-order history: the cold-start grinds with no diagnosis means gear engagement under cold oil was never inspected. Treat warm-up grinding as one startup problem. Safety floor: de-energize granulator and apply LOTO, hopper empty; no live transmission work. Next step: rotate gear by hand and feel for bind, measure backlash with feeler gauge, take warm oil sample — document hand-feel, backlash, oil grade — so you know if cold oil normal, too-tight mesh, or worn teeth.

Agitator seal is leaking again. Just a weep, stains the floor. Tightened packing nut last time and was OK for weeks.
Evidence (work-order history): 2026-05-12 tightened packing nut, leak stopped. 2026-07-09 weeping again.

Per the provided work-order history: seal weeping in weeks means packing compressing — the root cause was never found. Treat as one leakage problem. Safety floor: de-energize, stop rotation, apply LOTO before loosening; no live shaft work. Next step: measure how deep packing nut rotates by hand (write resistance), look at shaft for scoring, check speed rating on nameplate — log nut resistance, shaft condition, speed — so you know if natural wear, shaft damage, or above-rated operation.
